name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering (MathQA) datasets and 19 VQA datasets. Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation. In addition, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created to address missing types of mathematical reasoning over specific visual contexts. IQTest comprises 228 examples requiring inductive reasoning, abstract thinking, pattern prediction, and calculations, sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA, with 400 examples, emphasizes subtle visual perceptions of functional plots and algebraic reasoning. PaperQA is a novel dataset featuring questions derived from informative academic illustrations, including tables, figures, and charts from online education resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was collected from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets). For VQA datasets, examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. Three new datasets were created: IQTest (from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (functional plots and algebraic reasoning), and PaperQA (academic illustrations from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers released in August 2023 were used for PaperQA. The overall collection timeframe is not explicitly stated.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Three expert annotators then manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. Utilizing majority voting and limiting each source dataset to 400 examples, a collection of 2,739 examples was finalized. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the three newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For VQA dataset filtering, three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For metadata annotation of mathematical reasoning categories, expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven candidates to verify the quality of automatic annotation, achieving 94.1% exact match and 98.79% individual label accuracy.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom GUI annotation tool was developed for annotating the new source datasets and for labeling mathematical reasoning skills.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A two-step annotation process was employed to ensure consistency. Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Discrepancies (6 out of 736 questions) were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For mathematical reasoning category annotation, automatic and human annotations showed 94.1% exact match for the set of reasoning types and 98.79% individual label accuracy.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields annotated the three newly created datasets. For human performance baseline, eligible annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk must have a satisfactory annotating history, successfully pass qualification examples, and possess a high school degree or higher.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR was used for OCR text detection. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLMs. GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor from model responses.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that questions are biased toward North American educational standards and may not represent global curricula. English-only sources limit cross-lingual generalization. The dataset features 6.57% non-English questions, including languages such as Chinese and Persian, but the majority is in English.
rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The scalability and generalizability of the benchmark to other domains remain a concern. GPT-4V still falls short of human performance by 10.4%, and there is a significant gap between the best-performing model and human performance, indicating room for improvement.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used for training, testing, and validation of models. The benchmark is intended to facilitate the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks. The dataset is divided into two subsets: testmini (1,000 examples) for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources, and test (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation. Answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and an online evaluation platform will be maintained.
